Note: Rechargeable 3 V 1.5 mAh backup cell, reflow-solderable (as on SparkFun GPS-21834). Rated 10 uA at most; the switched-off GPS draws 28 uA, so it keeps satellite data for about a day at most. Farnell 3534555
TIA filter (~34 Hz). C0G/NP0 only. 1206 size: 100 nF C0G is hard to find in 0805
Stops the backup cell feeding the 3.3 V rail. Low-leakage type (0.5 uA max): a power Schottky leaks several uA back from the cell, on top of the GPS's own 28 uA
Flipper pins 1-8 (1 = 5V, 8 = GND). Holds the board. Through-hole. Any 2.54 mm right-angle 1x8 male header (e.g. X2530WR-08-PTSN)
JST PH 2.0 mm side-entry socket for the Grove GSR finger-cuff plug. Surface-mount; the two side tabs only hold it down
Flipper pins 9-18: 9 3V3, 11 GND, 13 USART TX, 14 USART RX, 15 PC1 SDA, 16 PC0 SCL, 18 GND. Through-hole

Also the GPS time pulse: joined inside the module to TIMEPULSE through 1k, so once the GPS has the time it goes high for 0.1 s at the start of each second. Short to TP6 (GND) at power-up for safeboot mode. Nothing may pull it low at power-up
Short to TP7 (GND) to reset the GPS. Clears its stored data: the next fix is a cold start

Zero-drift op-amp: offset under 10 uV, so the 0.5 V across the skin stays exact. Same pins as the MCP6002 on the prototype
